readScope: Final materialized reading of all 174 current question stems, all choices, answer keys and explanations on 2026-09-26; compared with corrected teaching and accumulated product/source reviews. This is a consistency and ambiguity pass, not independent certification.
findings: Broad triage stems can admit multiple reasonable actions or assessments because distractors are copied from other valid concepts.
Replaced six ambiguous triage items with specific scenarios, preserving IDs and lesson links.
Tightened three conjunctivitis scenarios and aligned question 017 explanation with diagnostic overlap. Remaining reviewed items retained; no claim of complete bank verification.
Allergy items 25–40 inspected. Replaced distractors in twelve items where unrelated valid advice could also apply. Retained correct teaching statements and four unambiguous principle items.

Reviewed items 41–64. Artificial-tear item 058 had near-duplicate correct options; replaced overlapping or broadly applicable distractors in nineteen items. Rewrote six explanations to address their actual question.

Reviewed prescription dry-eye items 65–76 against the product reviews. Replaced nine sets of broadly applicable alternatives and focused lifitegrast mechanism item 069 on the labeled molecular interaction while retaining mechanism uncertainty.

Reviewed items 77–96. Removed implication that steroid complications require inappropriate exposure; replaced thirteen overlapping distractor sets in items 78–92. Hydroxychloroquine items 93–96 retained provisionally pending complete current-guideline reconciliation.

Reviewed items 97–120. Replaced eighteen sets of overlapping administration, sterility and lens alternatives; made item 106 a product-specific 15-minute Restasis/lubricant case. Replaced three mismatched preservative explanations. General preservative teaching retained pending remaining lesson/source reconciliation.

Completed initial materialized reading of all 151 questions. Replaced nine overlapping alternative sets in items 121–132. Read all nineteen explicit product/infection cases; retained them against the existing product reviews, with final rendered checks still required. Independently recalculated 3.2 × 50 / 4 = 40 mg for the neonatal erythromycin case.
Reconciled items 93–96; replaced three broad items with specific screening questions. Expanded parafoveal-only wording to include pericentral toxicity.

Final 174-item reading found item 120 rationale incorrectly suggesting single-use handling universally; corrected to distinguish single-use and multidose instructions. Recomputed neonatal erythromycin dose: 3.2 × 50 / 4 = 40 mg. No additional conflicting correct answers identified in this pass.
